questions.q: What does the book say is the foundation of lasting business success?
a: Satisfied, engaged employees whose managers create the right culture
Aggressive cost cutting and frequent restructuring
A steady stream of new products and clever marketing
Strict procedures that keep every team member consistent
questions.why: Lesson 1 says profits follow loyal customers, who follow engaged employees.

questions.q: How should a manager handle standards and methods?
a: Set baseline standards, then let the team choose how to reach outcomes
Define every step of the process and audit it regularly
Let each employee set their own targets without any baselines
Copy the methods of the industry leader exactly
questions.why: Lesson 2 says processes matter less than outcomes once safety and accuracy are met.

questions.q: Why does the book say to study top performers rather than mistakes?
a: Studying mistakes leads to false conclusions and lower expectations
Top performers are easier to interview and observe
Mistakes are usually caused by factors outside work
Averages reveal more about a team than any individual does
questions.why: Lesson 3 warns that only observing weak nurses could make patient bonds look harmful.

a: Resentment and less engagement from the team
Faster decisions and stronger trust in leadership
Clearer standards and better-trained employees
More consistent outcomes across every project
questions.why: Lesson 2 says telling people exactly how to work makes them resentful.

questions.q: What are engaged employees more likely to do?
a: Treat customers well, stay longer and help save resources
Leave for competitors once their skills improve
Ignore company policy and set their own hours
Avoid responsibility for customer satisfaction
questions.why: Lesson 1 lists these behaviors as the payoff of genuine engagement.
